classes.name: Aura
classes.description:
The persistent effect of a [Spell] that remains on a [Unit] after the [Spell]
  has been cast.

As an example, if you cast a damage-over-time spell on a target, an [Aura] is
  put on the target that deals damage continuously.

[Aura]s on your player are displayed in-game as a series of icons to the left
  of the mini-map.

methods.description: Returns the ID of the [Spell] that caused this [Aura] to be applied.

methods.description: Returns the [Unit] that casted the [Spell] that caused this [Aura] to be applied.

methods.description: Returns the level of the [Unit] that casted the [Spell] that caused this [Aura] to be applied.

methods.description: Returns the amount of time left until the [Aura] expires.

returns.name: duration
returns.description: amount of time left in milliseconds

methods.description:
Returns the amount of time this [Aura] lasts when applied.

returns.name: max_duration
returns.description: the maximum duration of the Aura, in milliseconds

methods.name: SetMaxDuration
methods.description:

This does not affect the current duration of the [Aura], but if the [Aura]

params.name: duration
params.description: the new maximum duration of the Aura, in milliseconds

methods.name: SetStackAmount
methods.description:
Change the amount of times the [Aura] has "stacked" on the [Unit].

If `amount` is greater than or equal to the current number of stacks,
  then the [Aura] has its duration reset to the maximum duration.

classes.name: ElunaQuery
classes.description:
The result of a database query.

E.g. the return value of [Global:WorldDBQuery].

methods.name: GetBool
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to a boolean.

methods.name: GetColumnCount
methods.description: Returns the number of columns in the result set.

methods.name: GetDouble
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to a 64-bit floating point value.

methods.name: GetInt16
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to a signed 16-bit integer.

methods.name: GetInt32
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to a signed 32-bit integer.

methods.name: GetInt64
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to a signed 64-bit integer.

methods.name: GetInt8
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to a signed 8-bit integer.

methods.name: GetRow
methods.description:
Returns a table from the current row where keys are field names and values are the row's values.

All numerical values will be numbers and everything else is returned as a string.

**For example,** the query:

    SELECT entry, name FROM creature_template

would result in a table like:

    { entry = 123, name = "some creature name" }

To move to next row use [ElunaQuery:NextRow].

returns.name: rowData
returns.description: table filled with row columns and data where `T[column] = data`

methods.name: GetRowCount
methods.description: Returns the number of rows in the result set.

methods.name: GetString
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to a string.

methods.name: GetUInt16
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to an unsigned 16-bit integer.

methods.name: GetUInt32
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to an unsigned 32-bit integer.

methods.name: GetUInt64
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to an unsigned 64-bit integer.

methods.name: GetUInt8
methods.description: Returns the data in the specified column of the current row, casted to an unsigned 8-bit integer.

methods.name: IsNull
methods.description: Returns `true` if the specified column of the current row is `NULL`, otherwise `false`.

methods.name: NextRow
methods.description:
Advances the [ElunaQuery] to the next row in the result set.

*Do not* call this immediately after a query, or you'll skip the first row.

Returns `false` if there was no new row, otherwise `true`.

methods.description:
Returns a runtime-persistent cache tied to the [Map]. This data will remain for as long as the [Map] exists, or until a server restart. A reload of the Lua state will NOT clear this cache. This cache can be added to and read from with the following sub-methods. 
-- Sets the key-value pair in the cache

classes.name: Object
classes.description:
A basic game object (either an [Item] or a [WorldObject]).

Objects in MaNGOS/Trinity are stored an a giant block of "values".
Subclasses of Object, like [WorldObject], extend the block with more data specific to that subclass.
Further subclasses, like [Player], extend it even further.

A detailed map of all the fields in this data block can be found in the UpdateFields.h file of your emulator
  (it varies depending on the expansion supported).

The GetValue methods in this class (e.g. [Object:GetInt32Value]) provide low-level access to the data block.
Other methods, like [Object:HasFlag] and [Object:GetScale], merely wrap the GetValue methods and provide a simpler interface.

methods.name: GetByteValue
methods.description:
Returns the data at the specified index and offset, casted to an unsigned 8-bit integer.

E.g. if you want the second byte at index 10, you would pass in 1 as the offset.

methods.name: GetEntry
methods.description:
Returns the entry of the [Object].

[Player]s do not have an "entry".

methods.name: GetFloatValue
methods.description: Returns the data at the specified index, casted to a single-precision floating point value.

methods.name: GetGUID
methods.description:
Returns the GUID of the [Object].

GUID is an unique identifier for the object.

However on MaNGOS and cMangos creatures and gameobjects inside different maps can share
the same GUID but not on the same map.

On TrinityCore this value is unique across all maps

methods.name: GetGUIDLow
methods.description:
Returns the low-part of the [Object]'s GUID.

On TrinityCore all low GUIDs are different for all objects of the same type.
For example creatures in instances are assigned new GUIDs when the Map is created.

On MaNGOS and cMaNGOS low GUIDs are unique only on the same map.
For example creatures in instances use the same low GUID assigned for that spawn in the database.
This is why to identify a creature you have to know the instanceId and low GUID. See [Map:GetIntstanceId]

methods.name: GetInt32Value
methods.description: Returns the data at the specified index, casted to a signed 32-bit integer.

methods.name: GetScale
methods.description:
Returns the scale/size of the [Object].

This affects the size of a [WorldObject] in-game, but [Item]s don't have a "scale".

methods.name: GetTypeId
methods.description: Returns the TypeId of the [Object].

methods.name: GetUInt16Value
methods.description:
Returns the data at the specified index and offset, casted to a signed 16-bit integer.

E.g. if you want the second half-word at index 10, you would pass in 1 as the offset.

Returns a runtime-persistent cache tied to the [WorldObject]. This data will remain for as long as the [WorldObject] exists, or until a server restart. A reload of the Lua state will NOT clear this cache. This cache can be added to and read from with the following sub-methods. 
-- Sets the key-value pair in the cache
WorldObject:Data():Set("key", val)

-- Returns the value from the cache using the key
local val = WorldObject:Data():Get("key")

-- Removes the key-value pair from the cache
WorldObject:Data():Set("key", nil)

-- Returns all the key-value pairs as a Lua table indexed by the keys
local table = WorldObject:Data():AsTable()

globals.name: WorldDBExecute
globals.description:
Executes a SQL query on the world database.

The query may be executed *asynchronously* (at a later, unpredictable time).
If you need to execute the query synchronously, use [Global:WorldDBQuery] instead.

Any results produced are ignored.
If you need results from the query, use [Global:WorldDBQuery] instead.

    WorldDBExecute("DELETE FROM my_table")

globals.name: WorldDBQuery
globals.description:
Executes a SQL query on the world database and returns an [ElunaQuery].

The query is always executed synchronously
  (i.e. execution halts until the query has finished and then results are returned).

    local Q = WorldDBQuery("SELECT entry, name FROM creature_template LIMIT 10")
    if Q then
        repeat
            local entry, name = Q:GetUInt32(0), Q:GetString(1)
            print(entry, name)
        until not Q:NextRow()
    end

returns.name: results
returns.description: or nil if no rows found or nil if no rows found

globals.name: WorldDBQueryAsync
globals.description:
Initiates an asynchronous SQL query on the world database with a callback function.

The query is executed asynchronously, and the provided Lua function is called when the query completes.
The callback function parameter is the query result (an [ElunaQuery] or nil if no rows found).

    WorldDBQueryAsync("SELECT entry, name FROM creature_template LIMIT 10", function(results)
       if results then
           repeat
               local entry, name = results:GetUInt32(0), results:GetString(1)
               print(entry, name)
           until not results:NextRow()
       end
    end)

params.name: callback
params.description: the callback function to be called with the query results
